theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Real Estate (+2.21%) and Health Care (+1.39%) led the market today, while Energy (-0.13%) and Technology (-0.10%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged +0.21% versus +0.96% for defensives and +1.02% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.34% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.42%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps bucked the broader trend, with the Russell 2000 up +1.03%, outperforming large caps. The VIX rose 1.84% to 17.20, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 0.70% to $4,022.60, crude oil was little changed at $102.75, and bitcoin slipped 2.58% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
